model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: Model identity is the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, taken from the session environment (claude-opus-5[1m], Opus 5 with 1M context), not the agent definition's template text, which names claude-fable-5.

issues_detected.description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the record states the dataset is assembled from the clinical records of critically ill ICU, PICU and NICU patients at 14 hospitals, but no institutional review board, ethics committee of record, approval number or waiver determination is documented. ethical_reviews carries only the project's ethics workstream (community-facing focus groups on what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI), and human_subject_research.source_caveats concedes that 'the bundle does not state IRB approval for the dataset or name an ethics review board of record'.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the IRB(s) of record and the approval or waiver basis under which retrospective identifiable clinical records were extracted at each contributing site, harmonized centrally and made available to external users.

issues_detected.description: involves_human_subjects is true but there is no informed_consent slot anywhere in the record. For a retrospective multi-site extraction of patient records the expected statement is either a consent waiver, an opt-out arrangement, or consent obtained under a site protocol. direct_collection.is_direct is false with the explanation that data come from hospital systems 'rather than directly from patients', which makes the consent basis more important to state, not less.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add informed_consent stating the consent or waiver-of-consent basis for each contributing site, and whether patients can withdraw records already ingested into the enclave.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified is populated with a method (tokenization of unstructured text, transformation limiting re-identification, imaging de-identification), but there is no participant_privacy entry and no re-identification risk assessment. preprocessing_strategies asserts data are 'transformed using approaches that limit re-identification' without naming the approach, while sensitive_elements records social determinants of health together with geographic contextual factors, which are precisely the elements that raise re-identification risk in a critical care cohort.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the de-identification standard applied per modality (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, DICOM tag profile) and add an explicit residual re-identification risk assessment covering the geographic and social determinant elements.

issues_detected.description: third_party_sharing.is_shared is true and five distribution_formats are listed, but the record carries no download_url, no publisher, no repository accession and no access request URL. The only concrete access routes are a registration form belonging to one training program cohort and two email addresses recorded under data_governance.notes. A reader is told the data are released but not given a route to request them.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the standing data access request route (URL or named committee inbox) that applies outside the AIM-AHEAD training program, distinct from the cohort registration form.

issues_detected.description: license_and_use_terms describes terms attested only for participants in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program (a licensing agreement inside the registration form, a '.edu' address requirement), and its own source_caveats states that the bundle gives no general license for the data and no access terms outside that program. The reuse conditions for a general user are therefore undetermined even though the data are presented as released under controlled access.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the data use agreement that governs access outside the training program, or record explicitly that no general-access terms have been published yet.

issues_detected.description: updates describes growth from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions with imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process as of August 2025, but there is no version, no version_access and no errata. The 50,000-admission and 23 Tb figures cannot be attached to an identified release, so a user cannot say which snapshot their analysis used.
issues_detected.recommendation: Assign a release identifier to the currently accessible snapshot and record how prior snapshots are addressed inside the enclave.

issues_detected.description: id is https://chorus4ai.org/, the project homepage, which is also the value of page. A homepage is not a persistent identifier: it carries no registration, does not resolve to a version, and its content changes as the project grows toward the 100,000-admission target the record itself describes. No DOI, RRID or repository accession appears anywhere in the record, so there is no identifier format or registrar prefix to validate.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mint a DOI for the released snapshot, or record the enclave accession that identifies it, and keep the homepage in page only.

issues_detected.description: The program manager contact is recorded as 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu', whose domain is misspelled and does not resolve. The record transcribes it exactly as printed on chorus4ai.org and says so in source_caveats, which is the correct handling of a source defect, but the contact as recorded is unusable.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the verbatim transcription and add the corrected address alongside it, marked as a correction rather than as a source claim.

issues_detected.description: conforms_to_standard is the enumerated list [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER] while conforms_to names EDF+, Persyst, the OHNLP open-source schema and an extended PhysioNet waveform schema in prose. Three real, named standards are collapsed into the single token OTHER, so the machine-readable field under-specifies what the record's own prose states.
issues_detected.recommendation: Extend the standards enumeration, or carry the named standards in a structured per-modality list so the machine-readable field matches the prose.

issues_detected.description: Instance counts differ between the two sources and the record preserves both rather than silently reconciling them: 50,000 admissions on chorus4ai.org against 'over 45K unique admissions' as of August 2025 in the cohort 2 webinar, and 7,642 admissions with radiology data against 'currently 1000 images available'. The record states its ranking rule (project documentation preferred) and notes that the imaging figures count different things. This is accurate handling, but the released volume remains ambiguous by roughly 10 percent on admissions.
issues_detected.recommendation: Date-stamp each count to the snapshot it describes so the two sources are separated by release date rather than by source rank.

issues_detected.description: sampling_strategies reads 'Sampling designed to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies' and 'Federated access enabling sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort'. These are programme aspirations carried over from source prose, not a sampling design: no inclusion criteria, no site quotas, no balancing variable and no time window are given, and subpopulations.source_caveats separately concedes that no demographic breakdown exists.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the admission inclusion criteria and the date window per site, or state that the sampling design has not been published.

semantic_insights: The description is quantified and modality-resolved (50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb of waveform data) and separates the released dataset from the 100,000-admission anticipated dataset inline, so the reader is never left guessing which figure is current.

Per-modality standards are consistent across four different slots: conforms_to, distribution_formats, raw_data_sources and instances all agree that structured EHR is OMOP, imaging is DICOM, telemetry is WFDB, EEG is EDF+/Persyst and notes follow the OHNLP schema. That cross-slot coherence is unusual and it is what makes the interoperability claims credible.

The enclave architecture is described with its exception rather than as a slogan: clinical notes stay at the contributing site and only tokens move centrally, and the same fact reappears independently under confidential_elements, raw_data_sources, preprocessing_strategies, distribution_formats and known_limitations, where it is correctly named an integration limitation.

Grant identification is complete and internally consistent: award OT2OD032701, project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, USD 5,880,300 for fiscal year 2022, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30, with a well-formed RePORTER URL as the grant id.

Attribution is bounded rather than inflated: the record names Eric S. Rosenthal as the sole principal investigator per RePORTER and records the five other leadership figures as leadership team members with no PI role asserted, stating this in source_caveats.

The record declines to reconstruct a garbled table in the source PDF and says so, recording only the columns it could read. Declining to assert an unreadable per-modality metadata column is a correctness behaviour, not a coverage gap.

Ethics content is present but is the wrong kind for the sub-element it would satisfy: community focus groups and legal-landscape analysis are ethics research produced by the project, whereas the rubric asks for the oversight under which this dataset was assembled. The record itself flags the difference instead of letting the workstream stand in for approval.

Software transparency is real but is scattered: the chorus-ai organization, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-mapping, Chorus_SOP, chorus_waveform, CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool, CHoRUSReports and the OHNLP toolkit are all named, but they appear across external_resources, preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, machine_annotation_tools and extension_mechanism rather than in software_and_tools, and no version is given for any of them.

Temporal statements are ordered and mutually consistent: retrospective collection from existing records, dataset contents stated as of August 2025, a 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 project period, and a 2026-09-02 generation date.

correctness_validations.doi_format: not_present (no doi slot; id carries the project homepage https://chorus4ai.org/, and no RRID or repository accession appears anywhere in the record)
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: valid (OT2OD032701 follows the NIH pattern of activity code OT2, institute code OD and serial 032701; the full project number 1OT2OD032701-01 and application ID 10472824 are given, and the RePORTER project-details URL is well formed)
correctness_validations.url_validity: mostly_valid (https://chorus4ai.org/, https://github.com/chorus-ai, https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus, https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824 and https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema are all well formed; the maintainer contact cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu carries a misspelled domain, transcribed as published and explicitly caveated)

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; no doi, no rrid, no accession and no citation slot anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: The identifier is the project homepage, duplicated in page. It carries no registration, does not resolve to a version and will change as the dataset grows from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions. There is no DOI prefix and no RRID pattern to validate.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; name: CHoRUS; description of roughly 1,800 characters covering the consortium of 20 academic centers with 14 data acquisition sites, released counts (50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb waveform), the anticipated 100,000-admission dataset with 9 modalities, per-modality standards, the holdout test set, and the enclave with notes held on site
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the full program title and the short citable name are present. The description is quantified, modality-resolved, semantically appropriate for a multicenter critical care resource, and it distinguishes released from anticipated figures inline rather than blurring them.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 12 entries including 'critical care', 'intensive care unit', 'acute illness', 'electronic health records', 'OMOP Common Data Model', 'physiologic waveforms', 'electroencephalography', 'medical imaging', 'clinical notes', 'social determinants of health', 'Bridge2AI', 'AI-ready dataset'
sub_elements.quality_note: Twelve keywords, above the five-keyword threshold, spanning clinical domain, modality, data standard and program. Every term is discoverable and each is substantiated elsewhere in the record; none is filler.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; external_resources: chorus-ai GitHub organization (28 repositories, package status page, chorus-developer web guide) and the CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website; status field records the site's own modification-under-review banner
sub_elements.quality_note: A live landing page plus two substantive secondary resources. No hierarchical resources or file_collections structure is given, so a user learns where the project lives but not how the released files are organized.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: No parent_datasets and no related_datasets anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: CHoRUS is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and the record says so in prose, and it describes a sequestered holdout test set that is arguably a related release, but neither relationship is expressed as a typed link. Nothing machine-readable connects this dataset to any other.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: training program participants 'must sign a licensing agreement, included in the program registration form, before gaining access', with an institutional '.edu' address required; 'All data types are described as controlled access'. data_governance.access_review_process describes the registration, licensing and provisioning sequence and the email notification on approval
sub_elements.quality_note: A real and specific access policy with a named gate (signed agreement, .edu address, provisioned compute). Its scope is narrower than dataset-wide, which the record's own caveat concedes, but what is stated is concrete and actionable rather than boilerplate.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: No regulatory_restrictions and no confidentiality_level slot. human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance reads only that the project 'established a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape for clinical care AI'. confidential_elements records that notes stay on site and all data types are controlled access
sub_elements.quality_note: For identifiable US hospital records the expected statements are HIPAA status, the de-identification standard invoked and a sensitivity classification. None is present. The regulatory_compliance text describes a project activity, not a compliance status, and names no framework.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: No download_url. The only actionable routes are the AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 registration form described in prose and two access request addresses recorded in data_governance.notes; extension_mechanism.contribution_url points to the GitHub organization, which hosts tooling rather than data
sub_elements.quality_note: Controlled access does not excuse the absence of a request route: a controlled dataset normally publishes an application URL or a named committee inbox. Here a general user has no standing route, and the described route belongs to one training cohort.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: five entries covering OMOP CDM tables with flowsheet extensions, tokenized notes in the OHNLP schema, DICOM imaging from PACS, WFDB waveform telemetry under an extended PhysioNet schema, and EEG in EDF+ and Persyst, each with an access note and its published metadata schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality named in the description reappears here with a concrete format and its schema. The 23 Tb waveform volume is attached to the format entry, which is where a reuser would look for it.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: https://github.com/chorus-ai with a description enumerating chorus-mapping, Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-container-apps, CHoRUSReports and the chorus-developer guide; https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus
sub_elements.quality_note: The GitHub entry is a genuine documentation route, naming the specific repositories a reuser or contributor would need. No related_datasets are linked, so the sub-element is carried entirely by external resources.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats lists five populated modality entries, third_party_sharing.is_shared is true with the dataset 'made available beyond the contributing hospitals under controlled access', and data_governance.access_review_process describes a working access route. Under the ambiguity rule, approval-gated access counts as shared
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms describes only the training program licensing agreement and the '.edu' requirement; its source_caveats states 'The bundle states no general license for the data themselves and no access terms outside the training program context', and notes that the MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses on the chorus-ai organization apply to software repositories
sub_elements.quality_note: No reuse license exists for the data. The record is careful to separate the software licenses from the data, which prevents a reader from wrongly inferring MIT-licensed data, but the reuse permission itself is absent for anyone outside one training cohort.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above: distribution_formats populated and third_party_sharing.is_shared true
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; distribution_formats and raw_data_sources carry OMOP CDM, OHNLP schema, DICOM, WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema, and EDF+/Persyst
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality is expressed in a recognized community format and the same assignment holds across three slots. No character encoding is stated, and EDF+, Persyst and OHNLP collapse into the OTHER enum token, so the machine-readable list is thinner than the prose.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: prose mapping each modality to its standard, including 'schema extensions used for nursing flowsheets' and 'WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema'; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE ontology codes
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at the level a data engineer can act on, including where the standard is extended rather than adopted unchanged. The ontology codes on instances add machine-readable topic and substrate typing beyond the schema declaration.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot. instances describe row types ('Row of structured electronic health record data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, covering demographics, medication administration, provider-documented procedures and diagnoses, and high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation') but define no fields
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable, column or field-level metadata and no data dictionary. The OMOP reference implicitly carries the structured tables, but the flowsheet extensions are explicitly non-standard and nothing here documents them, which is exactly where a reuser would need variable definitions.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four categories (model development for acute and critical care, external validation against the sequestered holdout set, training and workforce development, equity and social determinants research) each with usage_notes or examples; existing_uses records training activities, the cohort 2 program and trainee outputs
sub_elements.quality_note: Intended uses are specific and tied to the dataset's actual construction, including the holdout set. No prohibited_uses and no discouraged_uses are recorded, which is a real gap for identifiable critical care data where re-identification attempts and clinical deployment warnings would be expected.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects condition met from E1 and E8 fields, not E4's own: description states the dataset comprises '50,000 patient admissions from intensive care units (ICU, PICU, and NICU)' assembled from contributing hospitals, keywords include 'critical care', 'intensive care unit', 'electronic health records' and 'clinical notes', and E8 collection_mechanisms describes 'Extraction from hospital electronic health record systems'
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[0]: 'Community-facing ethics focus groups are performed to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing', reviewing_organization 'CHoRUS consortium, Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar'; ethical_reviews[1] describes evaluation of community perspectives and analysis of the legal landscape. human_subject_research.source_caveats: 'The bundle does not state IRB approval for the dataset or name an ethics review board of record'. No data_protection_impacts
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics activity is documented; ethics oversight is not. There is no IRB of record, no approval or waiver, no reviewing board and no data protection impact assessment for identifiable records drawn from 14 hospitals. data_governance.committee_contact names a person with an email, but that is access administration rather than ethics review. The record is honest about the gap, which is the right handling and still leaves the sub-element unmet.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects condition as above, evidenced from E1 description and keywords and E8 collection_mechanisms
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text and transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification; de-identification of imaging'; deidentification_details records roughly 1,000 images available with de-identification in process, the privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid repositories, and that notes stay at the contributing site with only tokens released
sub_elements.quality_note: A concrete method per modality with named supporting tooling and an honest statement of what is still in progress. It falls short of naming a standard such as Safe Harbor or Expert Determination, and 'approaches that limit re-identification' is unspecific, but the architectural control of keeping notes on site is a real and verifiable measure.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects condition as above, evidenced from E1 and E8 fields
sub_elements.evidence: No participant_privacy entry and no reidentification_risk assessment. The nearest content is preprocessing_strategies 'Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification' and confidential_elements on note locality
sub_elements.quality_note: Access controls and tokenization are described, but no residual risk is assessed. That matters here because sensitive_elements records social determinants of health and geographic contextual factors alongside high-frequency waveform and EEG traces, all of which are recognized re-identification vectors in a critical care cohort. The record asserts risk limitation without assessing it.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects condition as above, evidenced from E1 and E8 fields
sub_elements.evidence: No informed_consent slot anywhere in the record. direct_collection.is_direct is false, with data 'obtained from hospital clinical systems ... rather than directly from patients'
sub_elements.quality_note: Nothing states whether consent was obtained, waived, or handled by opt-out at each site, and no withdrawal mechanism is described. For retrospective extraction of identifiable records this is the single most consequential omission in the element, and unlike the IRB gap it is not even flagged in a caveat.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human subjects condition as above, evidenced from E1 and E8 fields
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.special_populations: 'Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions' and 'Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions'; instances[0] records the admission type as ICU, PICU or NICU
sub_elements.quality_note: Vulnerable populations are identified explicitly and consistently with the cohort description, which is actionable for a reuser deciding whether pediatric review applies to their analysis. No protections specific to those populations and no participant compensation are recorded; compensation is arguably moot for retrospective records, but the additional safeguards for minors are not.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations[0]: subpopulation_elements_present true, identification 'Admissions in the released dataset are drawn from ICU, PICU, and NICU', source_caveats 'The bundle does not give the distribution of admissions across ICU, PICU, and NICU, nor any demographic breakdown of the cohort'
sub_elements.quality_note: The entry names three care settings and then states that nothing further is known. No age, sex, race, ethnicity or site distribution, no inclusion or exclusion criteria, and no counts per subgroup. The caveat is accurate and the content is too thin to characterize a cohort, which matters for a project whose stated purpose includes equity and social determinants research.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances: 50,000 hospital admissions (counts: 50000), 1,600,000,000 rows of OMOP-standardized EHR data, 7,642 admissions with radiology imaging, plus 23 Tb of waveform data recorded on the waveform instance; splits records the sequestered holdout test set
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are specific, typed by instance and attached to the modality they describe. Waveform and EEG instances carry no count, and the record says why for EEG (extraction in process). The conflicting webinar figure of 'over 45K unique admissions' is preserved with the ranking rule rather than dropped.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: No variables and no is_tabular slot. The OMOP instance describes its coverage in prose only
sub_elements.quality_note: The dataset is substantially tabular (1.6 billion OMOP rows plus flowsheet extensions) but neither the tabular flag nor any column-level description is present. A reuser cannot tell which OMOP tables are populated or how the nursing flowsheet extensions are shaped.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances carry data_topic codes B2AI_TOPIC:4, :9, :15, :37, :32 and data_substrate codes B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, :49, :43 across admissions, EHR rows, imaging, waveform, EEG and clinical notes; keywords add acute illness and social determinants of health
sub_elements.quality_note: Topic and substrate are machine-readable per instance rather than asserted once for the dataset, and the assignments are semantically appropriate for each modality. Specific disease conditions or phenotypes are not enumerated, so coverage is by care setting and modality rather than by diagnosis.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: No anomalies slot and no missing_data_documentation. sampling_strategies[0]: 'Sampling designed to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies across the multi-center network. Federated access enabling sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort'
sub_elements.quality_note: The only field populated is sampling_strategies, and its text is programme aspiration rather than method: no inclusion criteria, no site quota, no balancing variable, no time window. Nothing documents missingness in a dataset where high-frequency flowsheet and waveform capture make gaps certain, and no anomalies are recorded despite multi-site harmonization to OMOP.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met via E2 fields: distribution_formats lists five modality entries and third_party_sharing.is_shared is true, with access documented in data_governance.access_review_process
sub_elements.evidence: No version slot. status describes the release as 'Partially released under controlled access; data acquisition and curation ongoing'
sub_elements.quality_note: No version identifier of any kind for a dataset that is explicitly growing. The 50,000-admission and 23 Tb figures therefore describe an unnamed snapshot, and two users citing 'CHoRUS' may hold different data.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: No version_access slot; nothing describes how to reach an earlier snapshot inside the enclave
sub_elements.quality_note: With no versions declared there is also no route to a prior state, so an analysis run today cannot be reproduced against the data it used once ingestion continues.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: No errata slot. updates.update_details describes forward growth only and records no correction history
sub_elements.quality_note: No change log, no errata and no record of corrections, which is notable given that multi-site OMOP harmonization and imaging de-identification are both described as in progress and both routinely produce corrections.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: updates.update_details: 'The dataset is growing from the current released 50,000 admissions toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions and 9 data modalities across 14 contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were in process ... The NIH project period runs to 2026-11-30'
sub_elements.quality_note: A direction of travel and a funded end date, but no cadence, no release schedule and no maintenance commitment. A user cannot tell whether the next snapshot arrives in a month or at project end, which is what this sub-element asks.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: five entries naming hospital EHR systems for structured data and for notes (with access_details that notes stay local and only tokens move), hospital PACS in DICOM, bedside monitoring via gateway/middleware, and the hospital EEG database in EDF+ and Persyst; acquisition_methods describes site extracts prepared under validated SOPs and uploaded with chorus-extract-upload
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance from clinical system to released artifact is traceable per modality, including the tooling used at each hop. No was_derived_from link and no release_notes, so the provenance is narrative rather than a machine-readable derivation chain.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: five entries covering ML/AI support for characterizing acute and critical illness, an AI-ready dataset built with privacy and accountability, a holdout test set to aid marketplace adoption, ethically sourced datasets and best practices, and workforce development; addressing_gaps: three entries on critical care AI infrastructure, the multi-center acquisition challenge, and the absence of unified cross-modality standards
sub_elements.quality_note: Motivation is stated as a research gap with the specific deficiency named, not as a mission statement. The gaps map onto the dataset's actual construction: the standards gap explains the OMOP and WFDB harmonization, the infrastructure gap explains the enclave.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: characterizing acute and critical care illness; predicting complications and clinical deterioration; measuring treatment response; external validation against the sequestered holdout test set; labeling data with prediction targets in a visualization and annotation environment
sub_elements.quality_note: Five tasks that are recognizable ML formulations rather than restated purposes, and the holdout validation task is corroborated by the splits entry. The labeling task connects to labeling_strategies, so the objective and the mechanism are consistent.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health, NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; notes record the site's disclaimer that content is the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent official NIH views
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the agency and the specific funding program are named, and the OT2 award mechanism is visible in the award number. The NIH disclaimer is carried as a funder note, which is where a reuser looking for the sponsorship caveat would find it.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grants[0]: name 'OT2OD032701', id https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824, description giving project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, fiscal year 2022 award amount USD 5,880,300 and project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30
sub_elements.quality_note: The award number follows the NIH pattern exactly (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032701), and the full project number, application ID, amount and period are all consistent with each other and with a Common Fund Bridge2AI award. The RePORTER URL makes the claim independently checkable.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: created_by: 'CHoRUS consortium, a Bridge2AI data generation project'; creators: six entries, Eric S. Rosenthal as principal_investigator at Massachusetts General Hospital plus five leadership team members with affiliations (University of Florida, UTHealth Houston, Tufts University) and per-entry notes; maintainers names the program manager at MGH
sub_elements.quality_note: Attribution is bounded by evidence: the PI role is asserted only for the person RePORTER names, the other five are recorded as leadership team members, and source_caveats says so explicitly. That restraint is what makes the creator list trustworthy rather than merely long.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified and datasets shared: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms are populated, and the E2 datasets shared condition holds via distribution_formats and third_party_sharing.is_shared
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: five entries covering EHR extraction (demographics, medication administration at each infusion change or dose, provider documentation of procedures and diagnoses, high-frequency nursing flowsheets), PACS imaging extraction, waveform capture from bedside monitors via gateway/middleware, EEG extraction from the hospital EEG database, and note extraction and tokenization with the OHNLP toolkit; collection_timeframes and data_collectors record the retrospective window and the 14 contributing sites with their sub-team support
sub_elements.quality_note: One mechanism per modality with the source system named in each, at the granularity of the infusion-change timestamp. data_collectors distinguishes the contributing hospitals from the consortium sub-teams that support them, so the reader knows who did what.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: 'Retrospective extraction of clinical data recorded during routine hospital care ... delivered to CHoRUS as site-specific clinical data extracts prepared according to validated standard operating procedures and uploaded using the chorus-extract-upload tooling'; raw_data_sources names the five originating systems with formats and access details
sub_elements.quality_note: Instruments and route are both named, from the originating clinical system through the SOP-governed extract to the specific upload tool. The acquisition path is reconstructable by anyone with access to the named repositories.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software tools condition met via E10 external_resources, not E8's own fields: external_resources names the chorus-ai GitHub organization 'hosting 28 repositories of software and tooling', including chorus_waveform conversion scripts, chorus-mapping, CTP-deid and privacy_scan_tool
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: four entries (OMOP standardization with flowsheet extensions, note tokenization with OHNLP and site-local retention, transformation limiting re-identification, waveform conversion via chorus_waveform scripts); cleaning_strategies: characterization reports returned to each site (CHoRUSReports) and clinical validation of pooled semantic mappings under an SOP; labeling_strategies: a visualization and annotation environment for prediction targets; machine_annotation_tools: OHNLP toolkit with its output schema
sub_elements.quality_note: All four processing stages are populated, and the cleaning entries describe a real quality loop (site characterization feedback, clinician review of mappings) rather than a generic claim of validation. Annotation quality is the weakest link: an annotation environment is named with no inter-annotator agreement or quality analysis, and no imputation protocol is given.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same software tools condition as above, evidenced from E10 external_resources
sub_elements.evidence: No software_and_tools slot, but named tooling appears across the record: chorus-extract-upload, chorus-mapping, Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool, chorus-container-apps, CHoRUSReports, the chorus-developer guide, the OHNLP toolkit and the OHDSI tool stack, all reachable through https://github.com/chorus-ai
sub_elements.quality_note: The tools are real, individually named and resolvable, and each is tied to the step it performs, which is what the sub-element is for. Two defects: nothing carries a version, and the content sits in external_resources, preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools rather than the designated slot, so a machine consumer reading software_and_tools sees nothing.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met via E2 distribution_formats and third_party_sharing.is_shared
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: the chorus-ai organization with its package status page and developer guide, and the CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website; conforms_to names OMOP CDM, the OHNLP open-source schema, DICOM, WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema, and EDF+ and Persyst
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards and documentation routes are both present, and the standards are named at the level of the specific schema extension rather than the family. No published paper or protocol DOI is referenced, so the external record is code and documentation rather than literature.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: coverage_limitation (imaging de-identification in process with about 1,000 images available and EEG extraction in process as of August 2025), integration_limitation (notes held at contributing sites so full text cannot be analyzed alongside other modalities in the enclave), scope_limitation (retrospective ICU/PICU/NICU admissions at 14 hospitals, controlled access only)
sub_elements.quality_note: Three typed limitations, each naming a consequence a reuser would actually hit. The integration limitation is the strongest entry: it turns an architectural fact stated elsewhere into an explicit analytical constraint.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: No known_biases and no future_use_impacts slot. Bias appears only as project activity: ethical_reviews describes work to 'manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health', and intended_uses has an 'Equity and social determinants research' category
sub_elements.quality_note: No bias is categorized, named or assessed. The obvious candidates go unstated: 14 academic centers are not representative of US critical care, the cohort is ICU-selected, and the record's own subpopulations caveat concedes there is no demographic breakdown with which to check representativeness. Stating an intent to manage bias is not a bias disclosure.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: No anomalies slot. The nearest content is the coverage_limitation on in-process modalities and the source_caveats recording count discrepancies between chorus4ai.org and the cohort 2 webinar
sub_elements.quality_note: Incompleteness and source disagreement are documented, but no data-level anomaly is: no outliers, no site-to-site mapping inconsistencies, no gaps in waveform capture, nothing on the fidelity of the OMOP conversion. Those are the expected findings from the characterization reports the record says are produced for every site submission.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements[0]: sensitive_elements_present true, detailing patient-level clinical data from critically ill patients including demographics, diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, flowsheets, notes, imaging, waveform telemetry, EEG, and social determinants of health with geographic contextual factors; confidential_elements[0] records note locality and controlled access for all types
sub_elements.quality_note: The sensitive elements are enumerated by modality rather than summarized, and geographic contextual factors are called out explicitly, which is the disclosure a re-identification-aware reuser needs. No content warning is framed as guidance to a user, so the entry describes sensitivity without advising on handling.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries with reviewing_organization, covering community-facing ethics focus groups run by the Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, and consortium work on community perspectives, provenance and privacy trustworthiness, and the legal and regulatory landscape
sub_elements.quality_note: The entries are substantive and attributed to a named organizational unit, not boilerplate. What they document is ethics research rather than review of this dataset, and no conflicts of interest are disclosed for the creators or the contributing sites.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met via E2 fields: distribution_formats populated across five modalities and third_party_sharing.is_shared true with access described in data_governance.access_review_process
sub_elements.evidence: No publisher slot. The data live in a project cloud enclave; the only named platform is the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud, described under existing_uses as the training environment, and https://github.com/chorus-ai, which hosts software
sub_elements.quality_note: The dataset is not on PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo or any repository with its own persistent identifiers and access machinery, and no publisher of record is named. The enclave is real infrastructure but it is the project's own, so nothing external indexes this dataset.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication condition not met: there is no citation slot, and external_resources references only the chorus-ai GitHub organization and the CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website, neither of which is a publication reference. The datasets shared half of the condition holds, but both halves are required
sub_elements.evidence: No citation and no doi anywhere in the record; external_resources contains no article, preprint or protocol reference
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator: the condition requires a publication identified elsewhere in the record, and none is. The absence of a DOI is already scored against Element 1 sub-element 1, so scoring it again here would double-count the same defect.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to names OMOP CDM with flowsheet extensions, the OHNLP open-source schema, DICOM, WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema, and EDF+ and Persyst; conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance to five community standards across five modalities, each the dominant standard in its domain, plus the D4D schema declaration itself. This is the strongest integration claim in the element and it is corroborated by distribution_formats and raw_data_sources.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://chorus4ai.org/; external_resources describes the chorus-ai package status page, the chorus-developer web guide for contributors and users, and the Bridge2AI CHoRUS page; existing_uses describes the AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 training program with canonical Jupyter notebooks, the OHDSI tool stack, works-in-progress posters and annual meeting presentations; extension_mechanism describes the contributor workflow and its discussion spaces
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation for users and contributors is linked, and the training program with its notebooks and meeting presentations is genuine outreach with an audience and a timeline (up to 30 trainees, November 2025 to July 2026). No tutorial or webinar URL is given directly, so the reader reaches the material through the organization page.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: No related_datasets slot. The sequestered holdout test set is described under splits and purposes, and Bridge2AI sibling projects are alluded to only through the description phrase 'one of four data generation projects in the NIH Bridge2AI consortium'
sub_elements.quality_note: No relationship of any type is expressed to any other dataset. The holdout set is the clearest candidate, since it is a separately accessed artifact serving external validation, and the three sibling Bridge2AI generation projects are another. Neither is linked, so nothing places this dataset in its program's data landscape.

strengths: Per-modality technical transparency is complete and mutually consistent. Collection mechanism, acquisition route, raw source system, preprocessing step, standard and distribution format all agree for each of the five modalities, and the named tooling (chorus-extract-upload, chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, OHNLP toolkit, CHoRUSReports) makes the pipeline reconstructable rather than merely asserted.

Funding transparency is exact and independently checkable: award OT2OD032701 with project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, USD 5,880,300 for fiscal year 2022, a 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 period and a well-formed RePORTER URL, all consistent with a Common Fund Bridge2AI award.

Evidential discipline is visible throughout. Two sources are ranked rather than blended when their counts disagree, an unreadable table in the source PDF is declined instead of reconstructed, the PI role is asserted only for the person RePORTER names, a misspelled contact domain is transcribed as published and flagged, and the absent IRB is stated as a gap in the record rather than papered over.

The enclave architecture is documented as an analytical constraint, not a slogan: notes stay at contributing sites and only tokens move centrally, and that same fact reappears under confidential_elements, raw_data_sources, preprocessing_strategies, distribution_formats and, correctly, as an integration limitation in known_limitations.

Motivation, gaps, tasks and intended uses form a coherent chain. The standards gap explains the OMOP and WFDB harmonization, the holdout test set appears as a purpose, a task, a split and an intended use, and the equity purpose is matched by the social determinants elements recorded under sensitive_elements.
weaknesses: The human subjects basis is missing on both axes: no IRB or ethics committee of record and no approval or waiver, and no informed_consent slot at all, for a retrospective extraction of identifiable ICU, PICU and NICU records at 14 hospitals. The IRB gap is at least caveated; the consent gap is silent.

Privacy claims are asserted but not assessed. De-identification is described per modality, yet there is no participant_privacy entry and no re-identification risk assessment, while the record itself records social determinants of health and geographic contextual factors alongside high-frequency waveform and EEG traces.

Version tracking is entirely absent for a dataset the record says is growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions: no version, no version_access, no errata and no release cadence, so the counts and the 23 Tb waveform volume describe an unnamed snapshot that cannot be cited or reproduced.

Composition is thin below the modality level. No variables, no is_tabular flag, no demographic breakdown (conceded in the subpopulations caveat), no anomalies and no missing-data documentation, and sampling_strategies carries programme aspiration rather than a sampling design.

Reuse and integration are under-specified: no general license outside one training cohort, no download or access request URL, no publisher, no citation, no related_datasets and no bias categorization, so the dataset is presented as shared while offering a general user neither a route in nor terms to reuse under.
recommendations: Record the IRB(s) of record and the approval or waiver basis for each contributing site, and add informed_consent stating the consent, waiver or opt-out arrangement and any withdrawal mechanism for records already in the enclave.

Add participant_privacy with a named de-identification standard per modality (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, DICOM tag profile) and an explicit residual re-identification risk assessment covering the geographic and social determinant elements and the waveform and EEG traces.

Assign a version to the currently accessible snapshot, date-stamp each instance count to it, and record version_access and errata so the 50,000-admission figure and the August 2025 status statements attach to an identifiable release.

Publish the standing access route that applies outside the AIM-AHEAD training program, as a download_url or named committee inbox, together with the data use agreement that governs general access, and name a publisher of record for the enclave release.

Populate variables for the OMOP tables and the non-standard nursing flowsheet extensions, add is_tabular, and add known_biases covering the 14-center academic sampling frame, ICU selection and the demographic distribution the record currently reports as unknown.
